prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

A cassette type tape feeder including a tape feeding device that feeds a component supply tape to a component pickup position from a reel; a cover tape drawing-in device that peels off a cover tape from the component supply tape forward of the component suction position in accordance with a feeding operation of the component supply tape, and draws in the cover tape in a direction opposite to a feeding direction of the component supply tape; and a cover tape collection case that collects the cover tape drawn in by the cover tape drawing-in device. The cover tape collection case is configured of a fixing case section fixed to a cassette case, and a movable case section which expands capacity of the cover tape collection case by being displaced in a direction of the vacant space in the reel corresponding to an increase in collection amount of the cover tape. The movable case section is biased in a reducing direction by a torsion coil spring.

outputs.L2: A cassette-style tape feeder comprises a tape feed mechanism that advances a component supply tape from a reel to a component pick-up location; a cover-tape intake mechanism that, as the component supply tape is fed, separates the cover tape from the component supply tape at a point upstream of the component suction location and pulls the cover tape in a direction reverse to the supply tape’s feeding direction; and a cover-tape storage case that receives the cover tape taken in by the intake mechanism. outputs.L3:
A cassette-type tape feeder is configured to feed a component supply tape from a reel toward a component pickup position. The component supply tape carries electronic components at predetermined intervals and is advanced in a feeding direction so that each component can be presented accurately at the pickup position.

Before the component supply tape reaches the component suction position, a cover tape drawing-in device peels a cover tape from the component supply tape. This exposes the components held in the component supply tape, allowing them to be picked up by a suction nozzle or similar component handling device.

The cover tape drawing-in device pulls the peeled cover tape in a direction opposite to the feeding direction of the component supply tape. By drawing the cover tape backward relative to the advancing component supply tape, the device separates and guides the cover tape away from the component pickup area without interfering with the supply of components.

The peeled cover tape is collected in a cover tape collection case. As the cover tape drawing-in device continues to pull in the cover tape, the collected cover tape accumulates inside the collection case, keeping the feeder interior organized and preventing the tape from becoming tangled or obstructing operation.

The cover tape collection case includes a fixed section and a movable section. The movable section is biased by a spring and is configured to expand into vacant space within the reel area as the amount of collected cover tape increases. This structure allows the collection case to accommodate a growing volume of cover tape while making efficient use of available space inside the cassette-type tape feeder.
outputs.L4:
A cassette-type tape feeder is configured to supply electronic components to a component pickup position by feeding a component supply tape wound on a reel. The component supply tape includes a carrier tape having component storage cavities and a cover tape attached to the carrier tape to close the cavities. As the component supply tape is advanced from the reel toward the pickup position, the cover tape is peeled from the carrier tape so that the components stored in the cavities are exposed and can be picked up by a mounting head or other component transfer device.

After being peeled from the carrier tape, the cover tape is drawn in a direction opposite to, or away from, the tape feeding direction and is guided into a cover tape collection case provided within the cassette-type tape feeder. The collection case stores the peeled cover tape inside the feeder, thereby preventing the cover tape from interfering with tape feeding, component pickup, or surrounding equipment.

The cover tape collection case includes a fixed case section and a movable case section. The fixed case section is arranged at a predetermined position within the feeder body. The movable case section is supported so as to be displaceable relative to the fixed case section and is urged by a spring in a direction that increases the internal volume of the collection case. When the amount of collected cover tape is small, the movable case section can remain in a retracted position, allowing the collection case to occupy only a limited space inside the feeder.

As the feeder operates and the peeled cover tape accumulates in the collection case, the accumulated cover tape presses against the movable case section. The movable case section then moves against or under the force of the spring into a vacant space that becomes available inside the feeder as the component supply tape is unwound from the reel. In particular, as the diameter of the remaining tape wound on the reel decreases, an empty region is formed around the reel, and the movable case section expands into this empty region.

By allowing the collection case to expand into the vacant reel space created during operation, the feeder can increase the storage capacity for the peeled cover tape without increasing the external dimensions of the cassette-type tape feeder. This structure makes it possible to collect a larger amount of cover tape within the feeder while maintaining a compact feeder size. As a result, the need for frequent removal of accumulated cover tape is reduced, handling efficiency is improved, and the feeder remains suitable for use in high-density arrangements on a component mounting machine.
outputs.L5:
**The Power of “The”**

“The” is one of the smallest words in English, yet it plays a very important role. It is called a definite article, and it helps us talk about a specific person, place, thing, or idea. For example, when we say “the book,” we mean a particular book, not just any book. This simple word gives clarity and direction to a sentence.

Although “the” is easy to overlook, it appears everywhere in daily communication. We use it when talking about the sun, the world, the internet, the future, and countless other things. It helps connect ideas and makes language more precise.

In writing, “the” can also create emphasis. Saying “the best choice” or “the final moment” gives importance to what follows. Without this small word, many sentences would feel incomplete or unclear.

In short, “the” may be tiny, but it is essential. It shows that even the simplest words can have great meaning and purpose in language.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a patent-style abstract for a cassette type tape feeder that feeds component supply tape from a reel, peels and draws in cover tape opposite the feed direction, stores it in an expandable collection case with a movable section biased by a torsion coil spring.
counterfactuals.output: A cassette type tape feeder includes a feeder body configured to detachably support a reel on which a component supply tape is wound. The component supply tape includes a carrier tape holding components and a cover tape adhered to the carrier tape. A tape feeding mechanism feeds the component supply tape from the reel in a tape feed direction toward a component pickup position. A peeling mechanism peels the cover tape from the carrier tape, and a cover tape drawing mechanism draws the peeled cover tape in a direction opposite to the tape feed direction. The drawn cover tape is introduced into a cover tape collection case provided in the feeder body. The collection case includes a fixed section and a movable section defining a variable-volume storage space for the cover tape. The movable section is urged by a torsion coil spring in a direction to expand the storage space, thereby accommodating an increasing amount of collected cover tape while maintaining compactness of the feeder and stable cover tape take-in operation.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize the invention of a tape feeder for an electronic component mounting machine, including a tape feeding device, cover tape drawing-in device, collection case with fixed and movable sections, and spring-biased expansion into vacant reel space.
counterfactuals.output:
The invention is a tape feeder for an electronic component mounting machine that supplies components held in a carrier tape. It includes a tape feeding device that advances the component tape to a pickup position, and a cover tape drawing-in device that peels or draws the cover tape away from the carrier tape so the components can be accessed.

A distinctive feature is the cover tape collection case, which stores the removed cover tape. The case is made of a fixed section and a movable section. The movable section is biased by a spring so that it can expand outward into an otherwise vacant space originally intended for or left by a reel. As the amount of collected cover tape increases, the movable section shifts to enlarge the storage volume of the case.

This structure allows the feeder to collect a larger amount of cover tape without increasing the overall size of the feeder. By using unused reel-space efficiently, the invention reduces maintenance frequency, improves operability, and supports compact, continuous operation of the electronic component mounting machine.

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe a component supply tape cassette mechanism in formal patent language: it feeds tape to a pickup position, peels cover tape before the suction position, draws the cover tape backward, and collects it in a spring-loaded expandable case.
counterfactuals.output:
A component supply tape cassette mechanism comprises a cassette body configured to receive and guide a component carrier tape having component accommodating recesses sealed by a cover tape. The cassette body includes a tape feeding path extending toward a component pickup position at which components contained in the carrier tape are successively presented for removal by a suction nozzle or other pickup device.

A tape feeding mechanism is provided in the cassette body for intermittently advancing the carrier tape along the tape feeding path by a predetermined pitch corresponding to a spacing of the component accommodating recesses. The tape feeding mechanism may include a sprocket or feed wheel engageable with feed holes formed in the carrier tape, and a drive transmission portion adapted to be actuated by an external feeder drive or an internal drive source.

A cover tape peeling portion is disposed upstream of the component pickup position with respect to the direction of advancement of the carrier tape. The cover tape peeling portion is configured to separate the cover tape from the carrier tape before the corresponding component accommodating recess reaches the pickup position, thereby exposing a component to be picked up at the pickup position. The cover tape peeling portion may include a peeling edge, guide member, or turn-back member arranged to bend or redirect the cover tape away from the carrier tape at a predetermined peeling angle.

A cover tape drawing mechanism is arranged to draw the peeled cover tape in a direction generally opposite to the feeding direction of the carrier tape. The cover tape drawing mechanism guides the separated cover tape rearwardly from the peeling portion so that the peeled cover tape is prevented from interfering with the component pickup position and with the operation of the suction nozzle. The drawing mechanism may include one or more guide rollers, tensioning members, friction rollers, or a take-up drive portion for applying a rearward pulling force to the cover tape.

A cover tape collecting case is provided in or on the cassette body for receiving the cover tape drawn backward from the peeling portion. The collecting case includes an expandable storage chamber configured to accommodate an increasing length of collected cover tape as the carrier tape is consumed. A spring-loaded expansion member is associated with the collecting case and biases the storage chamber toward a contracted condition while permitting expansion of the storage chamber in response to accumulation of the cover tape therein. The spring-loaded expansion member maintains a restraining force on the collected cover tape so as to suppress loosening, entanglement, or outward escape of the cover tape.

Accordingly, during operation, the carrier tape is advanced to sequentially locate components at the pickup position, the cover tape is peeled from the carrier tape prior to arrival of each component at the pickup position, the peeled cover tape is drawn rearwardly away from the pickup position, and the peeled cover tape is accumulated within the spring-loaded expandable collecting case. This arrangement enables stable presentation of components to the suction position while compactly and reliably storing the removed cover tape within the cassette mechanism.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft an English abstract for a patent concerning a cover tape collecting structure in a cassette-type tape feeder, with a fixing case attached to the cassette case and a movable case biased by a torsion coil spring.
counterfactuals.output: A cover tape collecting structure for a cassette-type tape feeder is disclosed. The structure includes a fixing case mounted to a cassette case of the tape feeder and a movable case supported so as to be movable relative to the fixing case. A collecting space for receiving a cover tape peeled from a carrier tape is defined between the fixing case and the movable case. The movable case is urged by a torsion coil spring in a direction for reducing or closing the collecting space, thereby applying a pressing force to the collected cover tape. As the amount of collected cover tape increases, the movable case moves against the biasing force of the torsion coil spring to enlarge the collecting space. The cover tape can therefore be reliably accumulated in a compact manner within the cassette, while preventing loosening, scattering, or jamming of the cover tape and facilitating stable tape feeding and easy handling of the cassette-type tape feeder.
